title: CTS Parables of the Bible — Unit 6: The Unfaithful Wife — Unforgivable Forgiveness

blocks.en: 💍 Parables of the Bible — Unit 6: The Unfaithful Wife — Unforgivable Forgiveness
blocks.es_reference: 💍 Las Parábolas de la Biblia — Unidad 6: La Esposa Infiel — El Perdón de lo Imperdonable

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a lover and is committing adultery, just like the love of the LORD for the children of Israel." — Hosea 3:1 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Ve, ama a una mujer amada de su compañero, aunque adúltera, como el amor de Jehová para con los hijos de Israel." — Oseas 3:1 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: Some things seem unforgivable. Jeffrey Dahmer murdered at least seventeen young men and boys in the United States between 1978 and 1991. After he was convicted and sentenced to sixteen life terms, he claimed to have repented and was baptized in prison. Many people still find it almost impossible to imagine that such a man could be forgiven. His name remains one of the most unforgivable in American history.
blocks.es_reference: Algunas cosas parecen imperdonables. Jeffrey Dahmer asesinó al menos a diecisiete jóvenes y muchachos en los Estados Unidos entre 1978 y 1991. Después de ser condenado a dieciséis cadenas perpetuas, afirmó haberse arrepentido y fue bautizado en la cárcel. Mucha gente todavía encuentra casi imposible imaginar que un hombre así pudiera ser perdonado. Su nombre sigue siendo uno de los más imperdonables en la historia de los Estados Unidos.

blocks.en: The book of Hosea is about another seemingly unforgivable act: a woman who left her husband and children to go back to prostitution. Hosea's marriage is an enacted parable, like Jeremiah's visit to the potter's house in Unit 3, except that Hosea did not watch this sermon; he lived it for years. And it is the Bible's great example of what we may call unforgivable forgiveness: the forgiveness of what seems impossible to forgive. Hosea forgave Gomer. God forgave Israel. And God still forgives the unforgivable in us.
blocks.es_reference: El libro de Oseas trata de otro acto aparentemente imperdonable: una mujer que dejó a su esposo y a sus hijos para volver a la prostitución. El matrimonio de Oseas es una parábola actuada, como la visita de Jeremías a casa del alfarero en la Unidad 3, con la diferencia de que Oseas no vio este sermón; lo vivió durante años. Y es el gran ejemplo bíblico de lo que podemos llamar el perdón de lo imperdonable: el perdón de lo que parece imposible de perdonar. Oseas perdonó a Gomer. Dios perdonó a Israel. Y Dios todavía perdona lo imperdonable en nosotros.

blocks.en: I. The Setting
blocks.es_reference: I. El contexto

blocks.en: Hosea was an eighth-century prophet in the northern kingdom of Israel, a younger contemporary of Amos (Unit 4). He began to preach during the prosperous last years of Jeroboam II and continued through the chaos that followed, when kings were murdered one after another and the nation raced toward its destruction by Assyria in 722 BC (Hosea 1:1).
blocks.es_reference: Oseas fue un profeta del siglo octavo en el reino del norte de Israel, un contemporáneo más joven de Amós (Unidad 4). Comenzó a predicar durante los últimos años prósperos de Jeroboam II y continuó durante el caos que siguió, cuando los reyes eran asesinados uno tras otro y la nación corría hacia su destrucción por Asiria en el 722 a. C. (Oseas 1:1).

blocks.en: Israel's great sin was not that it abandoned the LORD completely, but that it wanted the LORD and Baal too. That sounds very open-minded; they wanted to be open to all religions. Baal was the Canaanite storm god, believed to send the rain that made crops grow. So Israel worshiped the LORD at the festivals and Baal in the fields, giving Baal credit for the harvest. God's complaint is heartbreaking: "She did not know that I gave her grain, new wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal" (Hosea 2:8). Israel treated God the way an unfaithful wife treats a faithful husband.
blocks.es_reference: El gran pecado de Israel no fue abandonar por completo a Jehová, sino querer a Jehová y también a Baal. Eso suena muy abierto de mente; querían estar abiertos a todas las religiones. Baal era el dios cananeo de la tormenta, a quien se le atribuía enviar la lluvia que hacía crecer las cosechas. Así que Israel adoraba a Jehová en las fiestas y a Baal en los campos, dándole a Baal el crédito por la cosecha. La queja de Dios parte el corazón: "Y ella no reconoció que yo le daba el trigo, el vino y el aceite, y que le multipliqué la plata y el oro que ofrecían a Baal" (Oseas 2:8). Israel trató a Dios como una esposa infiel trata a un esposo fiel.

blocks.en: II. A Marriage That Became a Message (Hosea 1:2–9)
blocks.es_reference: II. Un matrimonio que se convirtió en mensaje (Oseas 1:2–9)

blocks.en: God gave Hosea an astonishing command: "Go, take yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, for the land has committed great harlotry by departing from the LORD" (Hosea 1:2). Hosea married a woman named Gomer.
blocks.es_reference: Dios le dio a Oseas un mandato asombroso: "Ve, tómate una mujer fornicaria, e hijos de fornicación; porque la tierra fornica apartándose de Jehová" (Oseas 1:2). Oseas se casó con una mujer llamada Gomer.

blocks.en: Faithful interpreters understand this command in different ways, and students should know the options. Some believe Gomer was already a prostitute when Hosea married her; perhaps he loved her and hoped she would change, and her superficial faith soon gave way to her old habits. Others believe she was faithful at first and the phrase "wife of harlotry" describes what she became, since Hosea wrote the book looking back. A few have read the story as a vision or an allegory, though most evangelical interpreters take it as real events in a real marriage. On every reading, the heart of the parable is the same: Hosea's love for an unfaithful wife pictures God's love for unfaithful Israel.
blocks.es_reference: Intérpretes fieles entienden este mandato de maneras diferentes, y los estudiantes deben conocer las opciones. Algunos creen que Gomer ya era prostituta cuando Oseas se casó con ella; quizás él la amaba y esperaba que cambiara, y su fe superficial pronto cedió ante sus viejos hábitos. Otros creen que al principio fue fiel y que la frase "mujer fornicaria" describe lo que llegó a ser, pues Oseas escribió el libro mirando hacia atrás. Algunos pocos han leído la historia como una visión o una alegoría, aunque la mayoría de los intérpretes evangélicos la toman como hechos reales en un matrimonio real. En cualquier lectura, el corazón de la parábola es el mismo: el amor de Oseas por una esposa infiel representa el amor de Dios por el Israel infiel.

blocks.en: The couple had three children, and their names tell the tragedy. The first son was Jezreel, "God sows" or "God scatters," named for the valley where King Jehu had shed blood, and announcing that God would scatter the nation (1:4–5). The second, a daughter, was Lo-Ruhamah, "no mercy" or "not pitied" (1:6). The third, a son, was Lo-Ammi, "not My people" (1:9). Many readers notice that the text says Gomer "bore him a son" the first time, but does not say "him" for the second and third children. Hosea may have realized that he was not their father. By this time he knew he was sharing his home with a wife who was sleeping with other men.
blocks.es_reference: La pareja tuvo tres hijos, y sus nombres cuentan la tragedia. El primer hijo fue Jezreel, "Dios siembra" o "Dios esparce", nombrado por el valle donde el rey Jehú había derramado sangre, y anunciando que Dios esparciría a la nación (1:4–5). La segunda, una hija, fue Lo-ruhama, "no compadecida" (1:6). El tercero, un hijo, fue Lo-ammi, "no pueblo mío" (1:9). Muchos lectores notan que el texto dice que Gomer "le dio a luz un hijo" la primera vez, pero no dice "le" en el caso del segundo y el tercero. Quizás Oseas se dio cuenta de que no era el padre. Para entonces sabía que compartía su hogar con una esposa que se acostaba con otros hombres.

blocks.en: III. The Pain of a One-Way Love
blocks.es_reference: III. El dolor de un amor de una sola vía

blocks.en: Finally Gomer left. Hosea came home one day to three unsupervised children. She had gone back to her life as a prostitute, apparently enjoying the money and the attention. In chapter 2 the children are called to plead with their mother to come home, but even that was not enough. She was unfaithful to her husband, to God, and to her children. She did not have one lover but many.
blocks.es_reference: Finalmente Gomer se fue. Oseas llegó un día a casa y encontró a tres niños sin nadie que los cuidara. Ella había vuelto a su vida de prostituta, al parecer disfrutando el dinero y la atención. En el capítulo 2 se llama a los hijos a rogarle a su madre que vuelva a casa, pero ni eso bastó. Fue infiel a su esposo, a Dios y a sus hijos. No tenía un amante, sino muchos.

blocks.en: It is hard being in a one-way relationship. Most of us go through that at some point as teenagers. When I was in high school there was a girl named Sharon in our church youth group. She was cute and smart, and we did a lot of things together. I developed a crush on her, but it was evidently one-way. One day she came to me excitedly to tell me about a boy she had fallen for. I had to sit there and pretend it was great news. She wanted to be my friend, when the last thing I needed was another friend. That was a small taste of unrequited love. Hosea drank the whole cup, and so does God. Every time we give our hearts to something else, we treat the God who loves us the way Gomer treated Hosea.
blocks.es_reference: Es duro estar en una relación de una sola vía. La mayoría de nosotros pasamos por eso en algún momento de la adolescencia. Cuando yo estaba en la preparatoria había una muchacha llamada Sharon en el grupo de jóvenes de nuestra iglesia. Era linda e inteligente, y hacíamos muchas cosas juntos. Me enamoré de ella, pero evidentemente era de una sola vía. Un día vino a mí emocionada para contarme de un muchacho del que se había enamorado. Tuve que quedarme sentado y fingir que era una gran noticia. Ella quería ser mi amiga, cuando lo último que yo necesitaba era otra amiga. Esa fue una pequeña probada del amor no correspondido. Oseas bebió la copa entera, y también Dios. Cada vez que entregamos el corazón a otra cosa, tratamos al Dios que nos ama como Gomer trató a Oseas.

blocks.en: Sin also has consequences. "They sow the wind, and reap the whirlwind" (Hosea 8:7). Gomer got what she was looking for, but her beauty faded, and her life of adultery led her at last into slavery.
blocks.es_reference: El pecado también tiene consecuencias: "sembraron viento, y torbellino segarán" (Oseas 8:7). Gomer obtuvo lo que buscaba, pero su belleza se marchitó, y su vida de adulterio la llevó al fin a la esclavitud.

blocks.en: IV. God's Plan to Win Her Back (Hosea 2)
blocks.es_reference: IV. El plan de Dios para recuperarla (Oseas 2)

blocks.en: Chapter 2 begins like a divorce court: "She is not My wife, nor am I her husband!" (2:2). God threatens to strip away the gifts Israel credited to Baal. But in the middle of the judgment the tone changes. "Therefore, behold, I will allure her, will bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfort to her" (2:14). The Valley of Achor, the "valley of trouble" where Achan had brought disaster on Israel (Joshua 7), would become "a door of hope" (2:15).
blocks.es_reference: El capítulo 2 comienza como un tribunal de divorcio: "ella no es mi mujer, ni yo su marido" (2:2). Dios amenaza con quitar los dones que Israel atribuía a Baal. Pero en medio del juicio cambia el tono: "Pero he aquí que yo la atraeré y la llevaré al desierto, y hablaré a su corazón" (2:14). El valle de Acor, el "valle de la turbación" donde Acán había traído desastre sobre Israel (Josué 7), llegaría a ser "puerta de esperanza" (2:15).

blocks.en: Then comes a new wedding: "I will betroth you to Me forever; yes, I will betroth you to Me in righteousness and justice, in lovingkindness and mercy; I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness, and you shall know the LORD" (2:19–20). And the children's names are reversed. "I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; then I will say to those who were not My people, 'You are My people!' And they shall say, 'You are my God!'" (2:23). Paul and Peter both quote this promise to describe how God brought the Gentiles into His people through Christ (Romans 9:25–26; 1 Peter 2:10). "Not My people" becomes "My people." That is unforgivable forgiveness.
blocks.es_reference: Luego viene una nueva boda: "Y te desposaré conmigo para siempre; te desposaré conmigo en justicia, juicio, benignidad y misericordia. Y te desposaré conmigo en fidelidad, y conocerás a Jehová" (2:19–20). Y los nombres de los hijos se invierten: "tendré misericordia de Lo-ruhama; y diré a Lo-ammi: Tú eres pueblo mío, y él dirá: Dios mío" (2:23). Pablo y Pedro citan esta promesa para describir cómo Dios trajo a los gentiles a Su pueblo por medio de Cristo (Romanos 9:25–26; 1 Pedro 2:10). "No pueblo mío" se convierte en "pueblo mío". Ese es el perdón de lo imperdonable.

blocks.en: V. "Go Again, Love This Woman" (Hosea 3)
blocks.es_reference: V. "Ve, ama a esta mujer" (Oseas 3)

blocks.en: You might expect God to say, "Hosea, you have done all you can. Let her go. She made her bed; now let her lie in it." Instead God says, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by a lover and is committing adultery, just like the love of the LORD for the children of Israel, who look to other gods" (3:1).
blocks.es_reference: Uno esperaría que Dios dijera: "Oseas, ya hiciste todo lo que podías. Déjala ir. Ella tendió su cama; que se acueste en ella." En cambio, Dios dice: "Ve, ama a una mujer amada de su compañero, aunque adúltera, como el amor de Jehová para con los hijos de Israel, los cuales miran a dioses ajenos" (3:1).

blocks.en: Try to imagine the shock that command sent through Hosea's heart. On a personal level, should he set himself up to be hurt and humiliated again? On a religious level, as God's spokesman, how could he reverse his just condemnation of a woman who stood for Israel's sin? It went against everything he might have expected God to require. Yet he obeyed.
blocks.es_reference: Trate de imaginar el impacto que ese mandato causó en el corazón de Oseas. En lo personal, ¿debía exponerse otra vez a ser herido y humillado? En lo religioso, como portavoz de Dios, ¿cómo podía revertir su justa condena de una mujer que representaba el pecado de Israel? Iba en contra de todo lo que él podría haber esperado que Dios exigiera. Sin embargo, obedeció.

blocks.en: Historical sources tell us that slave markets in the ancient world were brutal places where human beings were treated like livestock. By the time Gomer was sold, she was no longer the beautiful woman Hosea had married. Hosea entered the bidding: "So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver, and one and one-half homers of barley" (3:2). Exodus 21:32 sets thirty shekels as the value of a slave. Hosea paid half of it in silver and made up the rest in barley, a humble price that shows how far sin had brought her down. And then he said, "You shall stay with me many days; you shall not play the harlot... so, too, will I be toward you" (3:3). She had been reclaimed by her own husband.
blocks.es_reference: Las fuentes históricas nos dicen que los mercados de esclavos del mundo antiguo eran lugares brutales donde los seres humanos eran tratados como ganado. Cuando Gomer fue vendida, ya no era la mujer hermosa con quien Oseas se había casado. Oseas entró en la subasta: "La compré entonces para mí por quince siclos de plata y un homer y medio de cebada" (3:2). Éxodo 21:32 fija treinta siclos como el valor de un esclavo. Oseas pagó la mitad en plata y completó el resto con cebada, un precio humilde que muestra cuán bajo la había llevado el pecado. Y luego le dijo: "Tú serás mía durante muchos días; no fornicarás... lo mismo haré yo contigo" (3:3). Había sido rescatada por su propio esposo.

blocks.en: Hosea's story is like the parable of the prodigal son, but with one striking difference. The prodigal "came to himself" and started home before his father ran to meet him. In Hosea 3 there is no mention of Gomer repenting first. The text simply says Hosea loved her again and went and bought her. Grace went looking for her. "God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8).
blocks.es_reference: La historia de Oseas se parece a la parábola del hijo pródigo, pero con una diferencia notable. El pródigo "volvió en sí" y emprendió el camino a casa antes de que su padre corriera a su encuentro. En Oseas 3 no se menciona que Gomer se arrepintiera primero. El texto simplemente dice que Oseas la amó de nuevo y fue a comprarla. La gracia salió a buscarla. "Mas Dios muestra su amor para con nosotros, en que siendo aún pecadores, Cristo murió por nosotros" (Romanos 5:8).

blocks.en: VI. Three Kinds of Unforgivable Forgiveness
blocks.es_reference: VI. Tres clases de perdón de lo imperdonable

blocks.en: 1. The unforgivable forgiveness of Israel. Hosea's book is the story of God's undying love for a people whose hearts had wandered far from Him. God cries, "How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel?... My heart churns within Me" (11:8). And the last chapter promises, "I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him" (14:4). Israel had been blessed with rich harvests, but instead of drawing the people back to their covenant, prosperity made them forget the Giver. Yet God would not let them go.
blocks.es_reference: 1. El perdón de lo imperdonable en Israel. El libro de Oseas es la historia del amor inquebrantable de Dios por un pueblo cuyo corazón se había alejado mucho de Él. Dios clama: "¿Cómo podré abandonarte, oh Efraín? ¿Te entregaré yo, Israel?... Mi corazón se conmueve dentro de mí" (11:8). Y el último capítulo promete: "Yo sanaré su rebelión, los amaré de pura gracia; porque mi ira se apartó de ellos" (14:4). Israel había sido bendecido con cosechas abundantes, pero en lugar de acercar al pueblo a su pacto, la prosperidad les hizo olvidar al Dador. Aun así, Dios no los dejó ir.

blocks.en: 2. The unforgivable forgiveness of us. Sin is spiritual adultery. Like Gomer, like Israel, and like us, anything that takes God's place in our hearts is unfaithfulness to Him. The word "backslide" means to turn back or turn away, and it seldom happens suddenly. Spiritual decay is a gradual process. Some time ago I was driving home from Tylertown along a road I knew well. I always turn at the house with the big windmill. That day I was thinking about something else, and I drove right past my turn. After a while everything looked strange. When I came to a four-way intersection I knew should not be there, I realized I was far down the Johnny Martin Road. But even after that detour, I was able to find my way straight home. We start out in the right direction and somehow get sidetracked. The good news is that we do not have to stay sidetracked. "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9). A young executive once asked the bank president he was replacing, "To what do you attribute your success?" "Two words," the president said: "good decisions." "But how did you learn to make good decisions?" "Two words: bad decisions." Failure is not final if we return to the Lord. God disciplines, but His ultimate aim is restoration, as the renaming of Hosea's children shows.
blocks.es_reference: 2. El perdón de lo imperdonable en nosotros. El pecado es adulterio espiritual. Como Gomer, como Israel y como nosotros, cualquier cosa que ocupe el lugar de Dios en nuestro corazón es infidelidad hacia Él. La palabra "apartarse" significa volverse atrás o desviarse, y rara vez sucede de repente. La decadencia espiritual es un proceso gradual. Hace algún tiempo yo volvía a casa desde Tylertown por un camino que conocía bien. Siempre doy vuelta en la casa del molino de viento grande. Ese día estaba pensando en otra cosa y pasé de largo. Después de un rato todo se veía extraño. Cuando llegué a un cruce de cuatro caminos que sabía que no debía estar allí, me di cuenta de que estaba muy lejos, en el camino Johnny Martin. Pero aun después de ese desvío, pude encontrar el camino directo a casa. Comenzamos en la dirección correcta y de alguna manera nos desviamos. La buena noticia es que no tenemos que quedarnos desviados. "Si confesamos nuestros pecados, él es fiel y justo para perdonar nuestros pecados, y limpiarnos de toda maldad" (1 Juan 1:9). Un joven ejecutivo le preguntó una vez al presidente del banco a quien iba a reemplazar: "¿A qué atribuye su éxito?" "Dos palabras", dijo el presidente: "buenas decisiones". "¿Pero cómo aprendió a tomar buenas decisiones?" "Dos palabras: malas decisiones." El fracaso no es definitivo si volvemos al Señor. Dios disciplina, pero Su meta final es la restauración, como muestra el cambio de nombre de los hijos de Oseas.

blocks.en: 3. The unforgivable forgiveness of others. Peter asked Jesus whether he should forgive a brother seven times, and Jesus answered, "up to seventy times seven" (Matthew 18:22). What about the person who betrayed you, lied about you, or stole from you? Isn't that unforgivable? We can forgive only with the same kind of love by which God loves us. Jesus prayed from the cross, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do" (Luke 23:34), and Stephen, as he was stoned, cried, "Lord, do not charge them with this sin" (Acts 7:60).
blocks.es_reference: 3. El perdón de lo imperdonable en otros. Pedro le preguntó a Jesús si debía perdonar a su hermano siete veces, y Jesús respondió: "aun hasta setenta veces siete" (Mateo 18:22). ¿Y la persona que lo traicionó, que mintió sobre usted o que le robó? ¿No es eso imperdonable? Solo podemos perdonar con la misma clase de amor con que Dios nos ama. Jesús oró desde la cruz: "Padre, perdónalos, porque no saben lo que hacen" (Lucas 23:34), y Esteban, mientras lo apedreaban, clamó: "Señor, no les tomes en cuenta este pecado" (Hechos 7:60).

blocks.en: For twenty-six years Margot Honecker, wife of East Germany's Communist leader Erich Honecker, ran the nation's Ministry of Education. Uwe Holmer was a Lutheran pastor at Lobetal, near Berlin, and time after time his children were refused places at the university, a common penalty for Christian families under that government. When the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, the Honeckers lost their power and their luxurious home. They found themselves friendless, with nowhere to go, and none of their old comrades would take them in. Pastor Holmer, remembering Jesus' words about turning the other cheek, invited them to live with his family in the parsonage. The Honeckers did not profess faith in Christ, but at meals they folded their hands and bowed their heads while the Holmer family prayed. That is unforgivable forgiveness.
blocks.es_reference: Durante veintiséis años Margot Honecker, esposa del líder comunista de Alemania Oriental Erich Honecker, dirigió el Ministerio de Educación del país. Uwe Holmer era pastor luterano en Lobetal, cerca de Berlín, y una y otra vez a sus hijos se les negó un lugar en la universidad, un castigo común para las familias cristianas bajo aquel gobierno. Cuando cayó el Muro de Berlín en 1989, los Honecker perdieron su poder y su lujosa casa. Se encontraron sin amigos y sin adónde ir, y ninguno de sus antiguos camaradas los quiso recibir. El pastor Holmer, recordando las palabras de Jesús sobre volver la otra mejilla, los invitó a vivir con su familia en la casa pastoral. Los Honecker no profesaron fe en Cristo, pero en las comidas juntaban las manos e inclinaban la cabeza mientras la familia Holmer oraba. Ese es el perdón de lo imperdonable.

blocks.en: VII. Mercy, Not Sacrifice
blocks.es_reference: VII. Misericordia y no sacrificio

blocks.en: Hosea also exposes religion that looks faithful on the outside. "For I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings" (Hosea 6:6). Jesus quoted this verse twice to religious leaders who criticized Him for eating with sinners and for showing mercy on the Sabbath (Matthew 9:13; 12:7). The Pharisees would have kept Gomer on the auction block. Jesus went to the market and paid the price. A church that understands Hosea will be known not for how carefully it keeps sinners at a distance, but for how gladly it welcomes them home.
blocks.es_reference: Oseas también desenmascara la religión que parece fiel por fuera: "Porque misericordia quiero, y no sacrificio, y conocimiento de Dios más que holocaustos" (Oseas 6:6). Jesús citó este versículo dos veces ante líderes religiosos que lo criticaban por comer con pecadores y por mostrar misericordia en el día de reposo (Mateo 9:13; 12:7). Los fariseos habrían dejado a Gomer en la subasta. Jesús fue al mercado y pagó el precio. Una iglesia que entiende a Oseas no será conocida por lo cuidadosamente que mantiene a distancia a los pecadores, sino por lo gozosamente que los recibe en casa.

blocks.en: VIII. Preaching Hosea
blocks.es_reference: VIII. Cómo predicar Oseas

blocks.en: A pastor can preach Hosea 1–3 under the title "Unforgivable Forgiveness," following three points: the unforgivable forgiveness of Israel, of us, and of others. Tell Gomer's story first, with the children's names and the slave market, so that listeners feel the scandal of God's command to "go again." Then turn the mirror: we are Gomer. Close with the invitation of 1 John 1:9 and the challenge to forgive others as we have been forgiven. Be careful and pastoral with this text. There may be listeners in your congregation who have been betrayed by a spouse, and Hosea is not a command that every betrayed spouse must stay in a dangerous or abusive situation. It is a picture of the relentless love of God.
blocks.es_reference: El pastor puede predicar Oseas 1–3 con el título "El perdón de lo imperdonable", siguiendo tres puntos: el perdón de lo imperdonable en Israel, en nosotros y en otros. Cuente primero la historia de Gomer, con los nombres de los hijos y el mercado de esclavos, para que los oyentes sientan el escándalo del mandato de Dios de "ir otra vez". Luego voltee el espejo: nosotros somos Gomer. Concluya con la invitación de 1 Juan 1:9 y el desafío de perdonar a otros como hemos sido perdonados. Sea cuidadoso y pastoral con este texto. Puede haber oyentes en su congregación que han sido traicionados por su cónyuge, y Oseas no es un mandato de que todo cónyuge traicionado deba permanecer en una situación peligrosa o de abuso. Es un cuadro del amor incansable de Dios.

blocks.en: Closing
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: The evangelist George Whitefield had a brother who had once been an earnest Christian but had fallen far from God. One afternoon, after hearing his brother preach, he sat at tea with Lady Huntingdon, unable to eat, and groaned, "I am a lost man." "I'm glad of it," she said. Astonished, he protested that it was cruel to say so. "I repeat it, sir," she said, "I am heartily glad of it, because it is written, 'The Son of Man has come to seek and to save that which was lost'" (Luke 19:10). With tears on his face he said, "What a precious Scripture! Then He will save me. I trust my soul in His hands." Charles Spurgeon, who told the story, said that he died shortly afterward, at peace with God.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelista George Whitefield tenía un hermano que en otro tiempo había sido un cristiano ferviente, pero que se había alejado mucho de Dios. Una tarde, después de oír predicar a su hermano, estaba sentado a la mesa con Lady Huntingdon, sin poder comer, y gimió: "Soy un hombre perdido." "Me alegro", dijo ella. Asombrado, él protestó que era cruel decir eso. "Lo repito, señor", dijo ella, "me alegro de corazón, porque está escrito: 'El Hijo del Hombre vino a buscar y a salvar lo que se había perdido'" (Lucas 19:10). Con lágrimas en el rostro, él dijo: "¡Qué Escritura tan preciosa! Entonces Él me salvará. Pongo mi alma en Sus manos." Carlos Spurgeon, quien contó la historia, dijo que murió poco después, en paz con Dios.

blocks.en: No one is beyond the reach of God's forgiveness. Hosea went to the slave market and bought back his unfaithful wife. God came to this world in Jesus Christ and paid the price for us, not with silver and barley, but with His own blood. That is unforgivable forgiveness, and it is offered to you today.
blocks.es_reference: Nadie está fuera del alcance del perdón de Dios. Oseas fue al mercado de esclavos y compró de nuevo a su esposa infiel. Dios vino a este mundo en Jesucristo y pagó el precio por nosotros, no con plata y cebada, sino con Su propia sangre. Ese es el perdón de lo imperdonable, y se le ofrece a usted hoy.

blocks.en:
— Dr. Wayne Cook
Chapala Theological Seminary

— Dr. Wayne Cook
Seminario Teológico de Chapala

mc.stem: This unit calls the story of Hosea and Gomer the Bible's great example of:
mc.why: Hosea forgave Gomer, God forgave Israel, and God still forgives the unforgivable in us.

mc.stem: Hosea's marriage is an enacted parable, but unlike Jeremiah at the potter's house, Hosea:
options: Lived the sermon for years instead of watching it
mc.why: Hosea's own home became God's message to the nation.

mc.stem: Israel's great sin in Hosea's day was that it:
options: Wanted the LORD and Baal too
mc.why: They worshiped the LORD at the festivals and Baal in the fields, crediting Baal for the harvest.

mc.stem: In Hosea 2:8, God complains that Israel did not know that:
options: He gave her grain, new wine, and oil
mc.why: Israel gave Baal credit for gifts that came from God.

mc.stem: Which is NOT one of the interpretations of "a wife of harlotry" presented in this unit?
options: Gomer was already a prostitute when Hosea married her
Gomer was faithful at first and became unfaithful later
Gomer was a priestess of the temple in Jerusalem
The story is a vision or allegory
mc.why: On every reading, Hosea's love for an unfaithful wife pictures God's love for Israel.

mc.stem: The name Lo-Ammi means:
mc.why: The third child's name announced the broken covenant; Hosea 2:23 reverses it.

mc.stem: Many readers notice that the text says Gomer bore "him" a son only for the first child, which may suggest:
options: The children were adopted from Judah
Hosea was not the father of the later children
mc.why: By then Hosea knew he was sharing his home with an unfaithful wife.

mc.stem: The story of Sharon in the church youth group illustrates:
options: The pain of a one-way love
mc.why: It was a small taste of unrequited love; Hosea and God drank the whole cup.

mc.stem: "They sow the wind, and reap the whirlwind" (Hosea 8:7) teaches that:
mc.why: Gomer got what she wanted, but her life of adultery led her into slavery.

mc.stem: In Hosea 2:15, the Valley of Achor, the "valley of trouble," becomes:
mc.why: The place of Achan's disaster becomes the doorway of God's restoring love.

mc.stem: Paul and Peter quote Hosea 2:23 ("You are My people") to describe:
options: God bringing the Gentiles into His people through Christ
mc.why: See Romans 9:25–26 and 1 Peter 2:10: "not My people" becomes "My people."

mc.stem: In Hosea 3:1, God told Hosea to:
options: Go again and love the adulterous woman
mc.why: "Just like the love of the LORD for the children of Israel, who look to other gods."

mc.stem: Hosea bought Gomer back for:
options: Fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley
mc.why: Exodus 21:32 values a slave at thirty shekels; Hosea paid half in silver and the rest in barley.

mc.stem: How does Hosea 3 differ from the parable of the prodigal son?
options: Gomer is not said to repent first; Hosea simply goes and buys her
Gomer returns home on her own
The prodigal is sold as a slave
mc.why: Grace went looking for her: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us (Romans 5:8).

mc.stem: "How can I give you up, Ephraim?" (Hosea 11:8) expresses:
options: God's undying love for unfaithful Israel
mc.why: This is the unforgivable forgiveness of Israel: God would not let them go.

mc.stem: The story of missing the turn and ending up on the Johnny Martin Road illustrates that:
options: Backsliding is gradual, but we can find our way back
We can never return once we stray
mc.why: "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us" (1 John 1:9).

mc.stem: Jesus told Peter to forgive:
mc.why: Matthew 18:22 calls us to the same kind of forgiving love by which God loves us.

mc.stem: Pastor Uwe Holmer showed unforgivable forgiveness by:
options: Refusing to pray for his enemies
Taking the Honeckers into his home after the Berlin Wall fell
mc.why: The family whose children were refused university sheltered the couple who ran that system.

mc.stem: Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6, "I desire mercy and not sacrifice," to religious leaders who:
options: Asked Him to offer a sacrifice
Criticized Him for eating with sinners and showing mercy on the Sabbath
mc.why: See Matthew 9:13 and 12:7: the Pharisees would have left Gomer on the auction block.

mc.stem: In the story of Whitefield's brother, Lady Huntingdon said she was glad he was lost because:
options: The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost
She wanted to end the conversation
mc.why: Luke 19:10 gave the backslider hope, and he trusted his soul to Christ.

fill.prompt: This unit calls Hosea's story an example of ____ forgiveness.
Israel wanted to worship the LORD and ____ too.
"They sow the wind, and reap the ____."
God said the Valley of Achor would become a door of ____.
God told Hosea, "Go ____, love a woman... committing adultery."
Hosea bought Gomer for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of ____.
Jesus told Peter to forgive up to seventy times ____.

sa.prompt: Explain what this unit means by "unforgivable forgiveness" and why Hosea's marriage is called an enacted parable.
sa.model: Unforgivable forgiveness is the forgiveness of what seems impossible to forgive. Gomer left her husband and children for prostitution, yet Hosea forgave her; God forgave unfaithful Israel; and God still forgives the unforgivable in us. It is an enacted parable because, like Jeremiah at the potter's house, the message came through actions, but Hosea lived this sermon in his own marriage for years.

sa.prompt: Describe Hosea's historical setting and Israel's sin with Baal.
sa.model: Hosea prophesied in the eighth century in the northern kingdom, beginning under Jeroboam II and continuing through the chaos before Assyria destroyed Israel in 722 BC. Israel wanted the LORD and Baal too. Baal was the Canaanite storm god believed to send rain, so Israel credited him for the harvest, though God said it was He who gave the grain, new wine, and oil.

sa.prompt: Present the main interpretations of God's command to marry "a wife of harlotry" and what all readings share.
sa.model: Some believe Gomer was already a prostitute when Hosea married her and that he hoped she would change. Others believe she was faithful at first and the phrase describes what she became, since Hosea wrote looking back. A few read it as a vision or allegory, though most evangelicals take it as real events. On every reading, Hosea's love for an unfaithful wife pictures God's love for unfaithful Israel.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of the three children's names and how Hosea 2:23 reverses them.
sa.model: Jezreel means God sows or scatters and announced judgment on the nation. Lo-Ruhamah means no mercy or not pitied, and Lo-Ammi means not My people. In Hosea 2:23 God reverses the names: He will have mercy on the one who had no mercy and say to those who were not His people, "You are My people." Paul and Peter apply this to the Gentiles brought into God's people through Christ.

sa.prompt: Describe Gomer's departure and explain how the Sharon story and Hosea 8:7 apply it.
sa.model: Gomer left Hosea and three children to return to prostitution, with many lovers, and even the children's pleading did not bring her back. The story of Sharon, a youth group crush who only wanted to be friends, gives a small taste of one-way, unrequited love; Hosea and God drank the whole cup. Hosea 8:7 says they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind: Gomer's sin led her at last into slavery.

sa.prompt: Explain God's plan to win Israel back in Hosea 2:14–20.
sa.model: In the middle of judgment God says He will allure Israel, bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfort to her. The Valley of Achor, the valley of trouble, becomes a door of hope. Then God promises a new wedding: He will betroth her to Himself forever in righteousness, justice, lovingkindness, mercy, and faithfulness, and she will know the LORD.

sa.prompt: Describe Hosea 3:1–3, including the price Hosea paid and why God's command was so shocking.
sa.model: God told Hosea to go again and love the adulterous woman, as the LORD loves Israel. It was shocking because Hosea risked being hurt and humiliated again, and as God's spokesman he seemed to reverse his just condemnation. Gomer had fallen into slavery, and Hosea bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley, half the thirty-shekel slave price in silver. She was reclaimed by her own husband.

sa.prompt: Compare Hosea 3 with the parable of the prodigal son and explain what the difference teaches about grace.
sa.model: In the prodigal son, the son came to himself and started home before his father ran to meet him. In Hosea 3 there is no mention of Gomer repenting first; Hosea simply loved her again and went and bought her. Grace went looking for her. This matches Romans 5:8: God showed His love in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

sa.prompt: Explain the three kinds of unforgivable forgiveness in this unit, with a Scripture or illustration for each.
sa.model: First, the forgiveness of Israel: God says, "How can I give you up, Ephraim?" and promises to heal their backsliding. Second, the forgiveness of us: sin is spiritual adultery and backsliding is gradual, like missing a turn, but 1 John 1:9 promises forgiveness when we confess. Third, the forgiveness of others: Jesus said to forgive seventy times seven, and Uwe Holmer took in the Honeckers who had persecuted his family.

sa.prompt: Explain Hosea 6:6 and how Jesus used it, and give one pastoral caution for preaching Hosea.
sa.model: Hosea 6:6 says God desires mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Jesus quoted it to Pharisees who criticized Him for eating with sinners and for showing mercy on the Sabbath. The Pharisees would have left Gomer on the auction block, but Jesus paid the price. A pastoral caution: some listeners have been betrayed by a spouse, and Hosea does not command anyone to stay in a dangerous or abusive situation.
